title: One-way ANOVA
biology: Ecologists compare seedling biomass under three independent soil treatments.
design: Twenty-five independently assigned pots per soil treatment; one biomass value per pot.
question: Are mean seedling biomasses equal across the three soils?
null: All soil-treatment population means are equal.
options: aov uses a shared within-group variance
An omnibus result does not identify a particular pair
assumptions: Approximately normal errors, especially at small n
Ordinary ANOVA assumes equal group variances
parametric: Welch ANOVA allows unequal group variances
Transform only if the new scale answers the scientific question
nonparametric: Kruskal–Wallis compares group distributions using ranks
Use adjusted follow-up comparisons that match the chosen method

plot_args.note: Use one persistent color per treatment
Show clearly labeled confidence intervals for means

practice: If you care only about Loam versus Sand, what follow-up quantity should you estimate?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1117)
d <- data.frame(soil = rep(c("Sand", "Loam", "Clay"), each = 25),
                biomass_g = c(rnorm(25, 4.5, .85), rnorm(25, 5.4, .85),
                              rnorm(25, 5.1, .85)))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
beeswarm(biomass_g ~ soil, data = d, pch = 21,
         bg = c("#246A73", "#B7663E", "#73649A"), col = "white", cex = 1.2,
         xlab = "Soil treatment", ylab = "Seedling biomass (g)")
means <- tapply(d$biomass_g, d$soil, mean)
se <- tapply(d$biomass_g, d$soil, sd) / sqrt(table(d$soil))
half <- qt(.975, df = table(d$soil) - 1) * se
segments(1:3, means - half, 1:3, means + half, lwd = 3)
points(1:3, means, pch = 18, cex = 2)
legend("topleft", "Mean and 95% CI", pch = 18, bty = "n")
code_analysis:
d$soil <- factor(d$soil, levels = c("Sand", "Loam", "Clay"))
fit <- aov(biomass_g ~ soil, data = d)
anova_table <- summary(fit)[[1]]
welch <- oneway.test(biomass_g ~ soil, data = d,
                    var.equal = FALSE)
generating_model: 25 independent biomass values per soil come from normal distributions: Sand mean 4.5, Loam mean 5.4, Clay mean 5.1 g; every group has SD 0.85 g.
generating_truth: The equal-means null is false. All three populations share variance 0.85 squared; Loam minus Sand is truly 0.9 g.

columns.name: biomass_g
columns.meaning: Seedling biomass from one independent pot

teaching_point: The omnibus equal-means question differs from a scientific question about one particular contrast.
